reason: Paul Nankervis's JavaScript 36-bit DECsystem-10 KI10 emulator, with floating-point, device I/O, front-panel controls, diagnostics and RP03 disk configuration for TOPS-10 v6.03A.

title: Flipull — Game Boy US/JP disassembly
reason: Annotated partial disassembly of the compact, mapperless Game Boy puzzle game; regional assembly generates US and Japanese ROMs and supports study of the level-49 kill screen.

title: miniscsi Macintosh SCSI driver
reason: Compact native Macintosh boot disk driver implemented in C with m68k assembly entry/header shim. Implements Apple partition scanning, registering/mounting HFS volumes, SCSI READ(10)/chunked WRITE(10), DriveStatus and drive icon in a position-independent raw driver.

title: osFree Janus Clock — Wine-derived native Win16 clock
reason: Wine Clock adapted to native Windows 3.x for Janus. Actual C drawing code creates analog hands/ticks and digital/time display; repository includes its own resources and makefile.

title: System Interrupt Demo V recovered source
reason: Preservation collection of System Interrupt demos I–V with actual recovered BBC BASIC/inline ARM implementation for Demo V v1.01, dated 5 February 1989. Only Demo V qualifies as source recovery; I–IV are contextual released binaries.

title: Pengu — native NGPC ice-block arcade game
reason: Original Neo Geo Pocket Color homebrew inspired by Pengo. C modules implement authored grids, sliding ice blocks, crush rules, hatching and pursuing Sno-Bees, wall stuns, lives and level timing. README explicitly says no original Pengo code, artwork, audio or data is used.

title: Wasteland IDE64 enhanced fix
reason: Binary-patching and replacement-loader project for C64 Wasteland, moving disk I/O to IDE64 and separating saves, fixing PAL/NTSC timing and turbo-speed behavior. Reviewed wasteland_fix.asm patches fixed-address game routines, requesters and interrupt vectors, and incorporates loader/fileops modules.

title: Z-MUSIC v2 X68000 sources and reconstructed variants
reason: Preserved/normalized source of Zenji Nishikawa's Z-MUSIC 2.08 driver/compiler/player plus rebuilt MZL 2.08e sources and later patched variants. Repository documents matching 2.08e from base sources and unified sources intended to reproduce original executables.

title: Tobu Tobu Girl
reason: Original arcade platformer with upward scrolling, timed stages, enemy bounces, dash/boost movement, unlockable skins, high scores and MML music. game.c implements concrete player/entity collision, spawning, level progress and native Game Boy video/audio control.

title: Drift — native OS/2 source continuation
reason: Dirk Vandenheuvel’s 1995 Asteroids-style Presentation Manager shooter, released as GPL source in 2002 and continued with an OpenWatcom build. Native C implements vector objects, shots, enemies, asteroid geometry and powerups, with keyboard, mouse and GAME$ joystick controls.

title: TwentyOne — native OS/2 source continuation
reason: Michael G. Slack’s 2001 Sibyl blackjack game translated to native C/OpenWatcom for OS/2. The rules implementation covers multi-deck shuffling, dealer/player scoring, splitting, doubling and insurance, with original Pascal retained.

title: Paybacktime 2
reason: Preservation of the 1994–1997 multiplayer, isometric, turn-based DOS tactics game by Niko Nevatie and Kari Luojus, including the game, editors and original Turbo Pascal/i386 assembler source.

title: Sadist (1998 DOS source)
reason: Author-published recovery of Grzegorz Drozd’s 1998–1999 Polish DOS game; the main Pascal implementation includes character physics, combat and environmental effects, with graphics, sound, mouse and XMS units.

title: Mastermind/2 — OS/2 single-executable source continuation
reason: Rene Auberger’s 1999 native OS/2 Mastermind game, with its legacy C source and a 2026 Open Watcom continuation that consolidates the language/resource DLL design into one executable. Source renders guess rows, drag/drop pins, exact/color-only feedback, timers and high scores.

title: TRS-80 Level II BASIC ROM reconstruction and enhancements
reason: Commented Z80 reconstruction of TRS-80 Model I/III Level II BASIC ROMs, with enhanced variants and EACA System-80 support. The author explicitly identifies the material as a derivative disassembly rather than original Microsoft/Tandy source.

title: LibVec — Vectrex assembly routine library
reason: Pre-alpha collection of reusable 6809 routines/macros for Vectrex vector drawing, timers, scoring, text, raw audio and DS2431 EEPROM. It adapts existing routines and some BIOS calls into macros to trade ROM space for cycles.

title: Fickle — VIC-20 one-button puzzle game
reason: Malcolm Tyrrell’s original 2011–2012 four-kilobyte real-time puzzle game for unexpanded VIC-20. One-button red/green mood switching controls whether the moving player responds to floor symbols, keys and switches.

title: Prospector in the Mazes of XOR remake
reason: Independent Java/PlayN implementation of the 1989 Amiga Prospector in the Mazes of XOR, compiled to an HTML5 browser game, with maze rules, renderer, editor and replay handling.

title: Rutgers ELISP — extended-addressing Lisp compiler source
reason: Charles Hedrick and colleagues’ extended-addressing Lisp preserved from Linköping tape images. Extracted source includes actual Lisp compiler, runtime/assembler modules and native TOPS-20 control scripts.

title: EarthBound / Mother 2
reason: ca65/spcasm source with US retail, localisation prototype and Japanese configurations. C decompilation is future work, not present completion.

title: Joe Blade DOS
reason: DOS COM disassembly with TASM-style source, includes and an IDA database. Generic labels and resource dependencies remain.

title: SNES Control Deck Tester
reason: Disassembly of the SELF TEST WCS diagnostic ROM using the author's SNES ROM Framework; requires original ROM for asset extraction.

title: PNG to PI1 — Atari ST picture converter
reason: Converts indexed 320x200 PNG pictures to Atari ST planar PI1, writes sixteen palette words and zeroed colour-cycle data, and checks a 32066-byte output length.

title: OGOL — C64 side-scroller
reason: Assembly side-scroller made for Arok party 2026 with scrolling, sword combat, effects and game assets. Inspected raster interrupt setup and gameplay source.

title: cr1901/REDos
reason: Tree includes a CLKDRV Binary Ninja database and original driver utilities, but no text analysis/export. Inspect the database in a supported read-only analysis environment or obtain exported findings before describing the actual reverse-engineering contribution; binary presence alone does not establish it.

title: OpenPCI — Amiga PCI abstraction
reason: Shared PCI enumeration, configuration, DMA and interrupt API with multiple bridge wrappers; library initialization and documented platform split inspected.

title: Dreamweb Assets — DOS resource extraction
reason: Parses Dreamweb room headers, graphics segments, object records, palettes, sounds and text into extracted resources. Inspected concrete room parser rather than relying on the asset-heavy tree.

title: SPR_EDIT — Atari ST GFA sprite editor
reason: Original sprite editor supports masks/automatic masking, drawing primitives, bitmap copy/paste and ICN export. Readable GFA listing and GEM resources are present.

title: GFA Fractals — historical ST map-animation tools
reason: Author archive contains Henon/Kaneko-style map applications, movie playback/save options and original tokenized GFA files with compiled programs.

title: GFA BASIC 3.6 — VS Code language support
reason: Syntax grammar, snippets, completion, hover documentation and procedure/symbol navigation for GFA listings. Inspected actual extension provider registrations.

title: Redsea — CPC pirate shoot-em-up
reason: CPCRetroDev 2018 original game with player/bullet/enemy logic, levels, maps and audio assets. Reviewed bullet state and movement implementation.

title: Final TAP Console — C64 tape-format scanners
reason: Historical Final TAP source has format-specific loader scanners, cleaning, CRC and extraction routines with tape-format documentation.

title: misterblack1/ef3-c64-tools
reason: README explicitly describes tools collected from the internet; tree provides bundled diagnostics rather than distinct source or analysis contribution.

title: New World Order — CPCTelera game
reason: Native game source includes player, ally/enemy animation and behavior, maps and build configuration.

title: Hole in One Professional — annotated MSX disassembly
reason: 32 KiB cartridge including course editor and opponent shot-simulation analysis. Primary build recipes and recursive Z80 tracing implementation inspected.

title: Konami’s Golf — annotated MSX disassembly
reason: 16 KiB cartridge; address-anchored notes, data walkers and graphics decompressors. Primary build recipes and recursive Z80 tracing implementation inspected.

title: ILBM Thumbnailer — KDE Amiga image previews
reason: KDE thumbnail plugin reads ILBM aspect information and uses ImageMagick for resized image display.

title: stuffandahalf/d64-c64
reason: README proposes a D64-to-drive transfer utility, but the complete implementation only parses help/version/baud options and exits. No image or transfer operation is implemented.

title: MacSD Classic II Toolkit — fork-preserving image builds
reason: Recipe-driven image builder/verifier preserves data/resource forks, Finder metadata and donor SCSI-driver bytes with independent filesystem checks.

title: ProDOS Disk Tool — IIgs text-image preparation
reason: Creates 2IMG/ProDOS images with text line-ending conversion and file metadata, with list/extract paths.

title: Macro HLA BASIC — structured 6502 macros
reason: ACME-style macro collection implements structured loops, conditions, integer helpers and stacks over native assembly.

title: a8tools — XEX disassembly and patching
reason: 6502 XEX disassembler uses memory maps, code/data/display-list sections and user symbols; PHP patcher supports game alterations.

title: atrfs — Python and Go Atari filesystem tools
reason: Parses ATR geometry and DOS directories with extraction, previews and evolving write operations; Go port normalizes short double-density boot sectors.

title: pbm2scr — monochrome Spectrum screen conversion
reason: Converts 256x192 PBM P1/P4 images into Spectrum screen-memory ordering.

title: spicyjack/Atari-8bit
reason: Collection preserves third-party ATASM and utilities; inspected assembler header credits Mark Schmelzenbach. ATASM already has a dedicated tracked project. No separate independent tool identity established for this root aggregation.

title: playptmod — ProTracker-derived replay library
reason: Self-contained MOD replay library derived from 8bitbubsy behavior reconstructed from ProTracker disassembly; includes multichannel and MTM extensions.

title: FlyDials — original GEM dialog library
reason: Historical flying dialogs, window/forms and font-selection helpers include Atari and contributed PC GEM paths.

title: taptool — Go Spectrum tape inspection
reason: Analyzes TAP headers/checksums, extracts BASIC and CODE data with manifests, and creates or appends loader/code blocks.

title: Commodore BASIC Code Editor — macro-enhanced source
reason: Editor rewrites labels, long variables, constants and compound assignments into numbered Commodore BASIC text.

title: MSX2 Tools — sprite, screen and bitmap editors
reason: Tkinter Spriter/Screener/Bitmapper suite prepares V9938 sprite patterns, maps and bitmap data, with BASIC detokenization utility.

title: DitherExtend — RISC OS disassembly and C port
reason: Restores Computer Concepts DitherExtend 0.60 as annotated ObjAsm and a routine-by-routine C module, covering dithering, blending and color-conversion SWIs.

title: libilbm — GIMP loader with obfuscated-chunk heuristics
reason: ILBM parser and GIMP loader recognize standard layouts and selected renamed chunk identifiers used in games such as The Clue and Whales Voyage.

title: Apple IIe Engine — graphics, speaker audio and assets
reason: Native graphics/sprite and one-bit audio experiment with modern bitmap/MIDI asset pipeline; main assembly structures and integration inspected.

title: Ayfly — AY replay library and desktop tools
reason: Cross-platform AY player/library includes tracker format dispatch, emulated Z80 replay paths, conversion and dumping frontends.

title: Chocolate Stunts — Restunts-derived native continuation
reason: Extends Restunts with native C DOS/SDL3 paths, original-assembly reference and replay verification, retaining explicit legacy-width arithmetic rather than a universal CPU interpreter.

title: Race into Space — released-source game restoration
reason: Reworks Buzz Aldrin’s Race into Space original released code, preserving game systems while replacing historical host integration.

title: Inner Worlds — early executable and resource investigation
reason: Investigates Inner Worlds 1.2 retail extender/file layout, resource tables and ELF details, with a C++ extraction prototype.

title: OpenVikings — partial Lost Vikings engine recovery
reason: Partial engine/data investigation includes level-header loading, planar graphics decoding, reverse-engineering notes and extraction scripts.

title: Martymations — Apple II animation reconstruction
reason: Annotated DEMOLIB disassembly identifies RLE image unpacking and even/odd-byte color-cycling animation used by Martin Kahn artwork hidden on Print Shop Color disks.

title: Petsciiator — Commodore image conversion
reason: Converts images into PETSCII screen/color data, BASIC and BBS output, plus Koala and Hi-Eddi formats with palette and dithering controls.

title: MSX Screen Converter — PHP image quantization
reason: Converts common image files to SCREEN 2/5/6/7/8/12 binary layouts with palette selection, dithering, tile and selected-region export.

title: kwankhhenry/PAL_Editor
reason: CMake skeleton and main returning zero do not implement the advertised DOS game data diagnosis.

title: Retrolarium Disassembler — multi-CPU ROM reconstruction
reason: Headless Ghidra pipelines recover bank-qualified instructions, pointer/dispatch structures and secondary CPU payloads, then emit modular assembler projects with rebuild manifests.

title: Sam-3Degrees/BBCSpriteEditor
reason: README describes planned architecture and canvas implementation is a placeholder; no implemented sprite editor established.

title: Apple II DOS 3.3 original-source archive
reason: Listed under original source listings in the SourceGen outbound index. The repository preserves original DOS 3.3 source and reference material; inspect its own annotations before claiming a distinct reverse-engineering project.

title: AMSDOS ROM listing in Amstrad-ROM-Sources
reason: The directory README says the author's own initial work was abandoned and the completed disassembly is an unidentified predecessor's work copied for discoverability; no distinct analysis by this repository is demonstrated for AMSDOS.

title: HAS (High Assembler)
reason: Python compiler for an assembly-first high-level language with typed control flow, inline assembly, macros, register control and Amiga libraries. hasc contains parser, AST, validators, code generator and optimizer; asset tools and examples remain part of this coherent compiler project. The compiler emits assembly and requires separately installed vasm/vlink for executables.

title: Outrun 2026
reason: Released CPC 6128 fan conversion based on Master System OutRun. Michel Louvet states Claude Code wrote a native Z80 engine and extraction/music tools, with measured tracks, scenery and handling and SN76489-to-AY music conversion. Author reports emulator and real-hardware testing. Inspected Outrun V0.8.zip contains only Outrun V0.8.dsk (194816 bytes); no source or patches were linked, so source availability/compilability and detailed architecture remain unverified. Claims of native rewriting and AI model identity are attributed to the author, not independently reproduced. Targeted public search checked the project and itch creator/profile links, Outrun/CPC/title and Michel Louvet/GitHub searches. No matching public source was found; the similarly named yonifra/outrun2026 repository is an unrelated HTML5 game.

title: benbaker76/jagfx
reason: Reusable Jaguar ROM graphics/compression searcher rather than a title-specific script.

title: avwohl/mbasic2025
reason: Primary source establishes a byte-identical reconstruction of the lost MBASIC 5.21 CP/M source.

title: Ali Baba reverse-engineering placeholder
reason: Pinned tree contains only README.md and .gitignore; no main.nw, main.pdf, source or build scripts exist, and releases are empty. README also mistakenly names a Lode Runner reference disk. No substantive Ali Baba reconstruction artifact was found; reconsider only if source is published.

title: Spy vs Spy Online
reason: README claims an Apple II-inspired Godot/Go multiplayer remake, but this pass has not implementation-reviewed the source or verified the original-platform fidelity, packaging or rights. Retained as an unpromoted lead.

title: ebadger/LunarMission
reason: GitHub repository metadata explicitly identifies this as a fork of 8bitclub/LunarMission. Its custom ebadger compiler-target changes do not create an independent game lineage; use canonical upstream.

title: JoeStrout/galactic-empire
reason: Static gameplay/source and specific Macintosh 68k ancestry reviewed; build/run/playable/byte-exact remain unknown.

title: Robotron: 2084 — ZX Spectrum annotated disassembly
reason: Primary repository documentation and inspected source establish a distinct in-scope retro-development project at the recorded scope.

title: SOTE Extractor — Shadows of the Empire asset archaeology
reason: Primary repository documentation and inspected source establish a distinct in-scope retro-development project at the recorded scope.

title: NeoWidEx
reason: Primary page establishes an Apple Lisa 2/10 Widget diagnostic and formatting utility, but implementation, build and exact runtime requirements need direct repository review before classification.

title: mnaberez/f2mc8dasm
reason: Primary documentation establishes a maintained F2MC-8 disassembler/reassembler with concrete identical-reassembly testing.

title: sarnau/sony-camera-protocol
reason: Primary documentation concerns the current Sony α7R V BLE/PTP-IP camera protocol and a Python client; it is reverse engineering, but not retro-development or legacy-software archaeology within this catalogue's scope.

title: chunkypixel/atari-dev-studio
reason: Primary repository evidence establishes a distinct in-scope retro-development or software-archaeology project; the matching project audit records CPU, build, runtime and uncertainty boundaries explicitly.

title: mdtools — Mega Drive graphics and music analysis
reason: Source expands the sparse README: mapping/DPLC tools, artwork splitting/recoloring, FM voice handling and SMPS-to-assembly conversion are present.

title: saprtools — cross-chip music conversion to POKEY
reason: Converts multiple chip/music formats into SAP-R and low-overhead POKEY playback. It explicitly does not make POKEY an exact SID/AY emulator; timer-driven effects, digidrums and rapid envelopes have limits.

title: Ocarina of Time — native Dreamcast port
reason: Native SH-4 port using recovered OOT game code, PowerVR display-list translation and AICA audio. Display-list interpretation is not MIPS CPU emulation. Only gc-eu-mq-dbg input is documented, not every retail ROM.

title: Mac::ResFork — classic Macintosh resource-fork parser
reason: Reads classic pre-OS-X resource-fork types, names and data. AppleDouble handling in inspected implementation assumes a fixed layout; do not infer full modern filesystem/container support.

title: PcW16 Typeface Preservation — pixel and metric capture
reason: Rosanne-native capture draws glyphs on white/black backgrounds, reads pixels and metrics, then creates BDF and pixel-outline TTF. It does not extract original scalable-font outlines. Captured fonts/OS files are not shipped.

title: AS Sonic — modified historical cross assembler
reason: Modified Macro-Assembler AS used by Mega Drive Sonic disassemblies. Includes genuine code generators, not game source itself; historical host portability statements are not current verified builds.

title: Astal — Saturn symbol maps and reversing tools
reason: US MK-81019 analysis publishes function maps, provisional names, Ghidra scripts and cross-overlay transfer tools, but no recovered C or game binaries. Zero placeholders is not semantic completeness; thousands of names remain provisional.

title: l1145a1/YOBJ-PSP-File-Structure-Documentation
reason: Detailed format notes with unknown fields, but no parser implementation, named game/version verification or validation corpus established. Retain as a format-research source rather than a working general PSP model toolkit.

title: Crossware 68000XR — BBC-hosted assembler disassembly
reason: Annotated reconstruction of the BBC sideways ROM for a 68000 cross assembler. Python explicitly loads the ROM as 65C02: 68000 is the generated instruction set, not the CPU executing this ROM.

title: Dekadence console tools — WonderSwan assets and checksums
reason: Converts MOD music and four-colour tile graphics, plus ROM checksum writing. Rust rewrite is explicitly unfinished; checksum generation performs no real ROM validation and overwrites input.

title: Parasite Eve II — USA matching reconstruction
reason: Upstream reports executable, two overlays and 446 packages matching. Preserve listed handwritten/inline assembly, register pins, assembler/linker-layout patches and unresolved semantic naming/types. A matching build is not a clean portable C-only port.

title: Tele-Ass — Oric Telestrat assembler ROM reconstruction
reason: ROM reconstruction has xa assembly, substantial byte tables and da65 code/data/label configuration. A byte-preserving representation is not equivalent to fully interpreted assembler internals.

title: Godzil/swancc
reason: Description proposes a WonderSwan C compiler, but inspected README/Makefile/compiler driver document inherited BCC/ELKS/PC8086 targets. Retain lead until WonderSwan-specific ABI/runtime/ROM output is evidenced; do not label a complete target toolchain from the repository name.

title: Golden Axe SMS editor — alpha asset tools
reason: Implements palette/tile/ROM data editing, but README warns of source-data corruption and unfinished compression writing, text editing and attribute rendering. Not a safe complete editor.

title: TubeXfer — BBC Tube fast-transfer OSWORD utility
reason: Single extensionless source file embeds assembler in BBC BASIC and installs OSWORD E0 transfer handling. Includes Tube claiming, parameter layout and presence/unload operations.

title: SEQ64 — N64 Music Macro Language tools
reason: V2 converts MIDI, textual MUS and binary COM/ASEQ/M64 music language with commands/loops and control flow. It no longer loads whole ROMs; legacyV1.5 serves that workflow.

title: Fortress of Necros — PC Engine English patch source
reason: Translation texts, character encoding notes and C text-formatting tool accompany the patch. Hardware/full-playthrough success is reported upstream, not independently verified here.

title: Dandaman955/Mega-Drive-Disassembly-Project
reason: Repository title promises all Mega Drive games but README narrows to incomplete Game Genie work; tree contains README and GameGenie.bin only. No inspectable source or disassembly established at this revision.

title: Taipan — Apple II rules reconstructed in Python
reason: New game code recovers original BASIC rules and formulas while replacing wording/art. Seeded Python RNG and formula tests do not prove identical original random sequences.

title: Ransom — Acorn C adventure implementation
reason: GAC sample adventure reimplemented in C on a BBC Master and refactored on A5000. Inspected extensionless C/gCode contains gameplay/counter/inventory interface. Do not infer6502 execution from BBC branding when Norcroft C environment is unspecified.

title: Spiral Wave — text extraction research
reason: Character-table and shifted-symbol decoding research. Source implements bytes-to-text but text-to-bytes is a pass stub; this is not a completed translation patch.

title: SG Edit Remix — Dragon/CoCo screen designer
reason: Browser low-resolution VDG screen editor exporting BASIC and6809 assembly. Inspected code generator emits actual drawing instructions plusFCBdata; target CPU describes generated code, not JavaScript host.

title: UEF2ROM — Electron cartridge conversion
reason: Converts cassette UEF data to cartridge/sideways ROM images with generated6502 loader code, persistent ROM pointer, tape-call interception and bank handling.

title: Yasu3D/SaturnEdit
reason: Modern SATURN rhythm-chart/cosmetics editor, not Sega Saturn hardware or software reconstruction. README and Avalonia project identify a name-match false positive, with no legacy-platform link established.

title: Manx TT Super Bike — Saturn analysis and symbols
reason: Function-name map, physics/archive/model studies and RNC tools, not distributed decompiled C. Source explicitly distinguishes symbol naming from a rebuilt executable.

title: lzexe — Rust DOS executable unpacker
reason: LZEXE 0.90/0.91/0.91e unpacker reconstructs MZ headers and relocation tables. Source returns a copied input for uncompressed data, so zero-copy wording must not be read as actual output behavior.

title: kumbach/maddictator
reason: AmigaOS3.2/SAS-C CNET BBS door WIP with setup/game-file/map rendering. Main UI command switch presently exposes map scrolling, help, quit and debug index; substantive conquest resolution not established by review. GPLv3 source; hold rather than claim playable game.

title: GEOS KERNAL original TASS-era predecessor
reason: 1999 TASS-era predecessor by the same author as already-tracked c64-geos2000; source/provenance value retained, no duplicate project counted. The original README describes changed booter/byte layout and dependency on the remaining GEOS system; its 99%-identical wording is not byte-exact proof.

title: lgbemu redistribution
reason: Primary README says this republishes Gábor Lénárt's Commodore LCD emulator with one crash fix and Python server instructions; that preservation/mirror-scale maintenance does not warrant a separate project record.

title: The Faery Tale Adventure original Amiga sources
reason: Repository explicitly publishes original Amiga Aztec C/68000 source rather than a reverse-engineered reconstruction. Valuable historical source archive, but outside a distinct RE record.

title: image-rider STX parser
reason: The example can extract STX track and sector data and the source implements parser scaffolding. README says formats are not fully parsed; included strictly as exploratory STX tooling.

title: Python-DICOM-tools
reason: DICOM/PACS Python utilities relate to medical imaging, not the tracker scope.

title: libexpat
reason: General-purpose streaming XML parser linked as a dependency of vscode-amiga-debug, with no legacy software analysis or platform-specific tooling in the repository description.

title: nrlpack
reason: PlayStation 2 executable packer; no demonstrated Amiga/Atari/C64/CPC or historical software recovery scope in reviewed files.

title: ulx3s_retro
reason: README surveys ULX3S FPGA retro-computing concepts; no original program analysis or distinct repository software artifact found in reviewed evidence.

title: sf2000-frogui-modded
reason: Modified FrogUI firmware front end for SF2000/GB300, based on prior frontend work; no original-game analysis or separate recovery tool shown.

title: DayzRally
reason: DayZ rally mission script, not historical software work.

title: Keyboard-FPC10
reason: Keyboard connector replacement PCB designed for Amstrad CPC; hardware only, with no software recovery or development tool.

title: LiteBSD
reason: 4.4BSD variant for PIC32MZ microcontrollers, not Atari or an original historical executable despite an Atari code-query hit.

title: elite-source-code-nes
reason: Copy of Mark Moxon's tracked NES Elite source, with three local commits adding build conveniences and two visual switches: simpler planet outline and hiding the scanner ELITE lettering. These are meaningful variant options, but no distinct source reconstruction or independent game project was established.

title: gimle-os
reason: The linked Attackwave/gimle-os URL returns 404. No primary artifacts available for qualification; Attackwave/m68k is separately tracked and should not be conflated with this inaccessible lead.

title: jotd666/bosconian

title: mcolom/arkanoid_msx_disasm
reason: The annotated source documents z80dasm provenance, a z80asm rebuild command and the expected rebuilt-ROM SHA-1.

title: Knight Lore CPC reconstruction
reason: RAM-derived CPC Knight Lore reconstruction contains symbolic Z80 assembly, data extraction and detailed engine analysis, with original and experimental rendering branches. Primary main-branch documentation reports successful RASM assembly and standalone snapshot boot to the real menu. This does not establish full playability or complete byte matching; the browser component is described only as a room visualizer.

title: Matrix mirrored listing
reason: README identifies mwenge/matrix and links its source/releases; no distinct contribution established in this pass.

title: Tearaway Thomas placeholder
reason: Root contains only .gitignore and LICENSE. Revisit when actual source or an author release appears.

title: 1kB Amstrad CPC games
reason: Collection of small CPC BASIC games including Moonlander, Emergency and Hanoi. Source listings are present alongside a disk image; kept as one coherent collection.

title: PongWIC64
reason: Network Pong with ACME C64 clients and Python host server. Author explicitly reports instability on real WiC64 hardware and success only in emulators.

title: Puyo Puyo Tsuu Mega Drive disassembly
reason: Early disassembly with build scripts and bytecode tables. Author explicitly warns it is not shiftable and not yet suitable for major projects.

title: The Puzzle Pits modernization

title: Ale Hop! — MSX disassembly

title: Pokémon Pinball — disassembly
reason: RGBDS disassembly with named screen state machine, engine, audio and data. README specifies a target ROM hash; no independent assembly performed.

title: King's Quest V native ST shim port
reason: Original Amiga binary converted and patched with game-specific AmigaOS/hardware shim plus PC EGA assets. Relevant native port, but hold for explicit compatibility/rehosting classification audit rather than label restored source.

title: Icebreaker 2 — 3DO original source
reason: Separate sequel source, developed after original but released in 2007. Historical .cp seeker logic/revisions distinguish it from Icebreaker; author release/licence claims attributed.

title: Chuckie Egg 2 — BBC Micro port
reason: 6502 port with original-code comparisons, room streaming for stock Model B and sideways-RAM edition. Sampled collision code explains a colour-dependent blind spot. Upstream runtime/hardware claims not independently verified; repository explicitly describes AI-assisted development.

title: ED-IT — TRS-80 Model 4 editor source
reason: Mark Reed editor sources covering commands, keyboard, display, disks, menus and printing. Main source identifies version 1.2 while README describes additions in 1.1; do not treat documentation version as current program version.

title: Motorola 68000 round-trip disassembler
reason: Standalone decoder targets reassemblable GNU AS/Sierra ASM68 output, presently focused on Mega Drive ROM hacking. Matching is the tool's goal; no independently verified universal round-trip guarantee.

title: AMOS Reborn — cross-platform BASIC runtime
reason: C/SDL2/OpenGL interpreter and graphics/audio modules informed by original AMOS source. Paula source explicitly approximates filtering. README overview and planned-feature list differ on browser support; no WASM target or cycle-accuracy claim promoted.

title: Heroes of the Lance — Master System disassembly
reason: In-progress commented Emulicious-derived listing with experimental modifications. Author warns commits can be unbuildable and output is not identical to original ROM; preserve uncertainty in comments.

title: Pit Fighter — Master System annotated disassembly
reason: Partial PAL-game exploration of size, graphics, menus and sound with annotated variables. Author explicitly disclaims full coverage and confidence in all interpretations; not a complete source restoration.

title: KKND — partial DOS matching decompilation
reason: Watcom matching project with substantive C replacements and many INCLUDE_ASM fallbacks. Byte-identical whole-image relinking does not mean the game is fully decompiled; upstream reports only a subset of functions replaced.

title: Ultima V Revolutions — Rust engine reconstruction
reason: Rust translation of DOS executable/overlay logic with original-file input and driver effect routines. User must supply game files; fidelity and all-function claims not independently verified.

title: Mega Man X4 PlayStation decompilation
reason: US executable reconstruction with typed engine/gameplay C and original-file extraction requirements. ROM/executable matching and completeness not independently tested.

title: SpecConv Spectrum analysis environment
reason: Interactive emulator/disassembler with coverage, persistent analysis and assembler/C export. README calls most analysis/decompilation features experimental; not proof of automatic complete C recovery.

title: A Link to the Past JP1.0 disassembly
reason: Annotated Japanese1.0 source and asset extractor using Futaba. Credits US disassembly and reused SPC work; not independent authorship of every component. Own ROM required for excluded binary assets.

title: Micro Machines Master System analysis and editor
reason: Named decompressor and broader disassembly alongside incomplete track editor. In-memory editing and compression exist; ROM reinsertion, layout auto-patching and several metadata editors remain unfinished. Keep coherent root project.

title: Acorn DFS 2.45 superseded disassembly
reason: README explicitly calls repository redundant and directs to tracked acorn_1770_dfs_disassembly covering 2.24/2.25/2.26/2.29/2.45.

title: PETSCII Robots CPC-named source
reason: README identifies ZX Spectrum 48K builds and main.asm declares device zxspectrum48 and savesna main.sna. Substantive game source exists, but advertised CPC adaptation or distinct lineage is not established. Do not assign CPC solely from repository name.

title: SMB Vanilla C reconstruction
reason: Actual C gameplay for SMB and Lost Levels with external ROM assets. Missing Lost Levels ending audio and regression tests remain explicit. README denies AI-generated code/assets and directs contributions to Codeberg; that narrower claim is not proof no AI was used for anything.

title: Aerobiz Supersonic Genesis disassembly
reason: Named68000 module source, ROM/RAM maps and byte-comparison workflow. Repository description says static recompilation but delivered goal/source is assembly reassembly. Complete naming and semantic-quality claims not independently audited.

title: Atalan retargetable 8-bit compiler
reason: Preserved/updated rule-driven compiler with actual basic-block optimization. Original author Rudla/Rudolf Kudla credited; abandoned origins, bugs and documentation drift explicit, not a polished maintained compiler claim.

title: Easier68k assembler and simulator
reason: Archived student-origin project with actual opcode assembly/execution code. Incomplete ISA/floating-point and accurate cycle measurement remain missing; not an accurate full-machine emulator.

title: Saboteur Spectrum standalone assembly
reason: Single-file annotated source with title-image decoder and ZX-M8XXX entry hints. Related SkoolKit presentation is already tracked and linked upstream; retain that relationship, not a claim of wholly independent reversing.

title: CP/M for Sega SG-1000 and SC-3000
reason: Proof-of-concept banked cartridge with writable first bank and CBIOS/terminal code. Disk access is read-only and requires compatible/modified emulator mapper; not an ordinary unmodified cartridge or hardware-verified port.

title: dax64 C64 assembly tools
reason: Assembler/disassembler and BASIC DATA extraction/loaders with VICE execution support. README explicitly excludes data areas in machine code and macro-style directives; not comprehensive round-trip analysis.

title: KSFL structured binary-format library
reason: Mac/Palm/PE/DFF/chunk-format APIs and CLI. Implemented Java MacResourceFile reviewed; other-language support is planned,not shipped by inference.

title: FamiTone 5 NES music driver
reason: Unofficial extension of Shiru's FamiTone2 with effects, full notes, volume columns and conversion tools. Requires its matching converters; fork false does not imply independent origin and it is not the original FamiTone2 project.

title: siddasm2 SID NSF SAP disassembler
reason: Music-container-aware 6502 disassembler for SID, NSF and SAP with load/init/play entry data. Successor to Gufino's earlier SID disassembler, not a whole-game decompilation or audio decoder.

title: Emerald Dragon PC Engine translation source
reason: Translation source, script compression and disc-build tools for Emerald Dragon. Existing dictionaries are cached and need regeneration after edits; CSV text comes from external editor workflow and original disc data is required.

title: ProDOS 8 read-only FUSE filesystem
reason: Linux FUSE reader for Apple II ProDOS 8 images with block/sector conversion. Author limits scope to personal small-disk recovery, excludes ProDOS 16 and warns of limited robustness. Internal block-write helpers do not establish a writable mounted filesystem.

title: RISC OS Python disassembler
reason: Capstone-backed ARM, Thumb and AArch64 decoding with RISC OS SWI/function and presentation conventions. Dependency-backed disassembler rather than a new CPU decoder; ARM64 support does not prove classic-machine execution compatibility.

title: Xenon 2 MSX2 sprite prototype
reason: Software-sprite/triple-buffer rendering experiment using Xenon 2 assets with mapped sprite pages. Concrete C/Z80 routines, not a full Xenon 2 game reconstruction or completed port. Stored prompt files alone do not establish completed AI authorship.

title: ALYNXDJ — original Atari Lynx music tracker
reason: Primary source for an original Atari Lynx music tracker with verified hardware builds, sample tooling and ComLynx/MIDI bridges.

title: Defender — ColecoVision disassembly
reason: Primary documentation and source establish a distinct, in-scope retro-development project.

title: Reverse-Engineering Azel RPG
reason: Substantive Panzer Dragoon Saga SH-2 disassembly/decompilation, disc analysis and progress evidence qualify independently of runnable status.

title: TRS-80 Diagnostic ROM — native RAM/VRAM test firmware
reason: Primary documentation and source establish a distinct, in-scope retro-development project.

title: VecForth — Vectrex Forth environment and 6809 cross-compiler
reason: Primary documentation establishes a CamelForth-derived Vectrex port, cross-compiler and standalone ROM workflow.

title: 9918 Adventures — TMS-9918 assembly starter and demo
reason: README declares a broad TMS-9918 family target list including SG-1000, SC-3000 and SF-7000. SG1000/Cart.s integrates startup/interrupt routines with shared title/game display code and outputs Burger.sg; batch recipe uses sjasmplus. Shared/GameZ80.s transfers compressed graphics and color tables into VRAM, supporting classification as a technical starter/demo. Development starter with shared display/graphics code, not a completed BurgerTime remake. Classified as tooling; multi-platform assembly starter and demonstration. README explicitly says the bolded systems, including SG-1000 and SC-3000, were tested on real hardware. Runnable=true records that attributed selected-platform claim only; it does not cover SF-7000 or every declared target. The sjasmplus batch success echo is not a test result; compilable/playable and byte exactness remain unknown. Development starter with shared display/graphics code, not a completed BurgerTime remake. Wider target list is retained as README declarations in notes. MIT root license does not replace third-party tool/asset licenses; Windows-specific recipes require path adaptation.

title: AmstradDSKExplorer — CPC DSK inspection and extraction
reason: Python 3 DSKInfoV3.py parses standard/extended CPC DSK headers, tracks, sectors and directory entries; includes disk creation, AMSDOS extraction and CP/M record-length extraction. README supplies working command examples; source history documents community disk testing and a Python 3.13 compatibility fix. Independent non-fork disk-image utility. Classified as tooling; disk-image inspection and file extraction. README supplies command examples and source history reports community disk tests and a Python 3.13 compatibility fix. No independently reproduced invocation or explicit current build success was established; flags remain unknown. Independent non-fork disk-image utility. No license file or explicit reuse grant was found in the inspected tree/source; provided-as-is wording does not establish an open-source license.

title: Crazee Rider — original BBC Micro source
reason: Author-released source adapted for BeebAsm; upstream build recipe available Kevin Edwards identifies this as his original 1987 racing game, detokenized from BBC BASIC inline assembly and adapted to BeebAsm. ROUT1.6502 implements input, game-state reset and vehicle control; MODULE.6502 contains BBC hardware IRQ and palette writes. Master.mak assembles separate game modules and emits the SSD image. The BBC and Electron roots are authentic machine-specific source versions, not duplicated mirrors. The BBC code includes raster palette changes absent from the Electron implementation. Author publishes converted original source for preservation; no explicit reuse license or LICENSE file was found. Public availability does not establish open-source permission. Documented build uses BeebAsm and a Windows make.bat wrapper. Supplied assembly, binary data and disk templates were inspected; no build, byte comparison, emulator or hardware execution was performed. Windows path/case assumptions should not be interpreted as a portable Unix build. This root covers BBC Micro only. The historical introduction mentions Master 128 and Electron, but that does not establish their source is included here.

title: LynxGDLib — Atari Lynx Game Drive cartridge I/O library
reason: Reusable cc65 library talks to Lynx Game Drive cartridge microcontroller through native registers and implements directory, seek, read, write and ROM-programming APIs. It is software development tooling rather than a board design. No standalone build script or independent hardware test. README says writes need a pre-existing memory-card file; correct LNX header EEPROM setting required. README provides integration/API examples but no standalone build or independent hardware test. Correct LNX header flags and a pre-existing file are needed for writes.

title: Sorcerers — native 64K CPC464 game
reason: Native homebrew potion/adventure game built with CPCtelera. Substantial main.c implements game states, rendering, input and end-game logic. The bundled Android APK is not evidence of an independently sourced Android reimplementation. Released one/two-player 64K CPC464 game source; native CPC build and gameplay not independently tested. Requires CPCtelera v1.5 development branch. Android APK is also present but is not a separately accepted port; only native CPC source is accepted. No build/runtime tests performed. Top-level license and README describe GPL v3/GPL, but main.c header says LGPL v3-or-later; retain the inconsistency. Castle artwork is adapted from Freepik with attribution terms.

title: Sorcery+ Remake — incomplete MonoGame remake and room editor
reason: Game1.cs implements a native MonoGame game loop and coordinates world state, item, enemy, room and collision systems; no game-specific CPU emulation wrapper. Current room registry contains nine authored rooms; older README Phase-1 and docs five-room counts are stale. Recent commits explicitly record Claude co-authorship; .claude project guidance and agent files reinforce AI-assisted development evidence. Native source reimplementation with SorceryForge; no guest CPU execution wrapper was identified. Classified as subject; native C#/MonoGame reimplementation with editor. Game1.cs, item/room systems and SorceryForge editor are substantial native C#/MonoGame code. Current registry has nine rooms; Phase-1 and five-room documentation is stale. Missing energy/death/lives, timer, cauldrons, audio and much of the world prohibit a complete-game claim. No build/play flags are asserted. Native source reimplementation with SorceryForge; no guest CPU execution wrapper was identified. README claims MIT and a LICENSE file, but none is present in the recursive tree. Newer asset documentation/Content entries contradict the README claim that original assets are excluded: extracted sheets/backgrounds are present with separate rights.

title: CodeTree — C64/6502 control-flow graph analysis
reason: Parses C64 RAM from VICE VSF snapshots or PRG files, follows 6502 control flow, and emits Graphviz call graphs. Optional Regenerator configuration supplies code/data segmentation and labels; the actual parser and control-flow implementation were inspected. User-supplied entry points and forced stops are required; README explicitly warns that paired complementary conditional branches are not recognized as an unconditional jump. This is an offline analysis tool, not a native game or a proof of correct whole-program decompilation.

title: Picross — C64 4K puzzle-game source
reason: Author identifies this as a Reset C64 4K competition entry. Assembly contains puzzle state, row/column handling, cursor input, completion checks and KERNAL-backed saving; puzzle/font data is represented in source. Build script calls a hardcoded external VBS label-converter helper, plus Exomizer and c1541. No license is provided; competition-entry description does not establish redistribution rights or a tested final release.

title: Squid Jump — native C64 fan recreation source
reason: Substantial assembly implements charged jumps, gravity, sprite/collision handling, score and rising water with level data. Source has PAL/NTSC timing constants and selects 50 versus 60 frames. Repository metadata only says port of Squid Jump; original-game source lineage and asset rights were not established. No README, license or complete build script occurs in the inspected tree; do not claim complete, buildable or playable verification.

title: claude-api-suno-api-music-gen-pipeline
reason: General AI music-generation pipeline, no retro-platform recovery or analysis.

title: electrobots-releases
reason: Original modern Electron/BBC game distributed as tape/disk and executable images; no source-recovery or development-tool output in this release repository.

title: Soft968-Amstrad-Firmware-Manual
reason: Hyperlinked CPC firmware manual, useful to verify firmware/jumpblock semantics but not an implemented analysis tool.

title: radareorg/radare2
reason: General-purpose multi-platform reversing framework; the README gives no distinct legacy-platform project or extension to track here.

title: Mutant Monty — native Amiga Scorpion conversion
reason: Creator-published Scorpion source contains substantial Mutant Monty game logic, actors, 41 level maps, graphics and sound, with released Amiga ADF/WHDLoad builds linked from the creator page. It qualifies as a native fan conversion; original C64/CPC binary analysis is not claimed.

title: Atari_ST_Sources original-source archive
reason: Large collection of existing Atari ST assembly and C source trees. The archive alone does not establish a distinct binary-to-source reconstruction project; review a specific contained project separately if authored reverse-engineering evidence appears.

title: Super Mario Bros. — SourceGen conversion
reason: The author ports doppelganger's existing disassembly and says he has not meaningfully modified the original analysis. Pattern-table visualizers are useful but this is not a separate original game disassembly.
